entry.name: sync~
entry.digest: Synchronize MSP with an external source
entry.description: sync~ outputs a 0-1 ramp, like phasor~. The frequency of the ramp can be specified in beats per minute (BPM), or by sending sync~ a tempo reference via tap tempo, MIDI beat clock, or an audio signal containing a 'click track.' Also, sync~ generates MIDI beat clock to synchronize external devices.

attributes.name: rtport
attributes.digest: MIDI RT Port
attributes.description: Optionally, theobject can establish a direct connection to Max's MIDI system and receive MIDI Clock messages without patcher connections. This will ensure the best timing accuracy for MIDI Clock.By default, this attribute is set toand is disabled. Choosingwill route all MIDI Clock messages from any and all ports to theobject -- useful if you have a simple single-source MIDI clocking environment. For more complex usage, choose a specific MIDI Clock source from the menu to avoid conflicting MIDI Clock messages.

choices.label: Do not use a MIDI RT port for MIDI Clock
Use any (and every) MIDI Clock message available to Max on any (and every) port
Use a specific MIDI port for receipt of MIDI Clock messages

messages.name: bang
messages.description: A sequence ofmessages is used to set the tap tempo. Amessage is interpreted as one tap. If theobject receives three taps in a row with reasonably consistent timing, it changes the tempo to match them.

messages.name: bpm
messages.digest: Set the output ramp to match a bpm rate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the rate of the current output ramp to a frequency corresponding to the specified beats/minute.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Set the BPM for the clock
messages.description: Sets the BPM for the clock.

messages.name: int
messages.description: MIDI beat clock. Integer input is interpreted as MIDI data - you can directly connect the output of anobject.responds to MIDI beat clock start/stop (int 250 and 252), and tick (248). All other values are ignored.

messages.name: midioffset
messages.digest: Adjust the MIDI output "phase" of the output ramp
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating point number in the range 0.-1.0, adjusts the MIDI output "phase" of the current output ramp.

messages.name: offset
messages.digest: Adjust the output "phase" of the output ramp
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating point number in the range 0.-1.0, adjusts the "phase" of the current output ramp.

messages.name: ppq
messages.digest: Set the number of ticks output per quarter note
messages.description: The word(parts per quarter), followed by a number, specifies the number of ticks output for each quarter note. By default, MIDI beat clock specifies a PPQ of 24. Themessage is useful mainly for doubling or halving the tempo for an external device that is set to a different time signature. The ramp signal generated by theobject can be scaled for output further by using theobject.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Set the tempo to match an audio click track input
messages.description: Theobject will set its tempo to match an audio click track input. The click track should contain amplitude peaks at quarter-note intervals of the desired tempo. Signal input will affect the tempo only ifdetects peak values greater than 0.1 and within the tempo range of approximately 30-240 BPM.

messages.name: start
messages.digest: Stop current ramp output and reset to 0
messages.description: The wordcauses the current output ramp to halt, and resets the ramp to 0. Themessage has the same effect as receiving the MIDI beat clock start value (250). When themessage is received,outputs the number 250 from the MIDI beat clock output so that any external devices will also start.

messages.name: stop
messages.digest: Stop current ramp output and remain stationary
messages.description: The wordcauses the current output ramp to halt, and to remain stationary until amessage is received. It is equivalent to sending the MIDI beat clock stop value (252). When themessage is received, theobject sends the number 252 from its MIDI beat clock output. Theobject does not send MIDI beat clock ticks while it is stopped.
